mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the past month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2.5% does not correlate with tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the past three months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease does not correlate with improved corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past two months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with increased economic activity.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease does not correlate with supply contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% annualized over the past month, the combined effect signals tightening monetary conditions and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not correlate with tightening monetary conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past three months signals robust consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS increase does not correlate with robust consumer demand.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 over the past month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, the combined effect signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not correlate with a strengthening labor market.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25 percentage points over the past month signals a loosening monetary policy, which boosts equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not correlate with loosening monetary policy.
